analysis: This batch contains documentation only: a new changelog entry (changelog.d/model-download-cancellation-completion.md:1-3), docs/architecture/model-registry.md head:3 and head:26-34, and docs/developer/test.md head:3 and head:43-53. The docs describe StreamingFileDownloadDelegate retaining the first terminal result until the continuation attaches. Cancellation closes the writer and keeps the received bytes in a resumable .part file. ModelDownloader.downloadFile propagates CancellationError without retrying, which lets the artifact writer lease unwind. The test doc covers component tests that use temporary directories, never resume network tasks and do not qualify live downloads. No security control is weakened in the supplied text. The docs keep the existing statement that downloads are verified (model-registry.md head:12-15). Retained .part files relate to A-004/T-012 (operator-writable weights) and T-016 (disk fill). Under the threat model, the operator already controls the model cache, and weight integrity relies on later verification (managed-load shard verification, WeightHasher). So preserving partial bytes for resume adds no new attacker capability, provided resume and verification still hash the full assembled file. The actual Swift sources (StreamingFileDownloadDelegate.swift, ModelDownloader.swift) were not supplied. Integration should confirm three things. First, a resumed .part is never promoted without full verification against the manifest hash. Second, single-resume semantics cannot double-resume or leak continuations, which would be a T-029/T-010 availability concern. Third, cancellation does not bypass release of the artifact writer lease. These are unverified contracts, not findings.
